# SetWindowSizeLimit

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzPlus](BlitzPlus) · [Windows](BlitzPlus-Windows)

</div>


```blitzbasic
SetWindowSizeLimit:Void window:Int32, min_width:Int32, min_height:Int32, max_width:Int32, max_height:Int32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | In | Int32 | required | Handle of a window that can be resized. |
| `min_width` | In | Int32 | required | Smallest width, 0 for no limit. |
| `min_height` | In | Int32 | required | Smallest height, 0 for no limit. |
| `max_width` | In | Int32 | required | Biggest width, 0 for no limit. |
| `max_height` | In | Int32 | required | Biggest height, 0 for no limit. |

## Description

A BlitzLLVM extension: sets how small and how big the user may make a window. Windows holds the window to these sizes while the user drags an edge, and [SetGadgetShape](SetGadgetShape) keeps to them as well. A size of 0 means no limit there. It replaces what [SetMinWindowSize](SetMinWindowSize) set.

## Differences

* Not in the original, which only has [SetMinWindowSize](SetMinWindowSize) and lets a window grow as big as the desktop. A program there that keeps a window smaller has to shrink it back after the user resized it.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
win = CreateWindow("Only wider", 20, 20, 240, 160, Desktop(), 15)
SetWindowSizeLimit win, 160, 160, 480, 160 ; Between 160 and 480 wide, always 160 high.
Repeat
Until WaitEvent() = $803
```
